# Preprocessing {#sec-data-cleaning}
The main processing of data is splitted into three parts: data cleaning[^clearning], the inclusion of 
additional data[^additional_data], and the aggregation of invidiual trips to generate a dataset for NN and SVM
[^aggregation].

[^clearning]: 01_data_cleaning.ipynb
[^additional_data]: 02_other_data_sources.ipynb
[^aggregation]: 03_data_preparation_for_nn_and_svm.ipynb


## Data Cleaning
In this step, the raw taxi trip data [@chicago_taxi_trips] is processed to a cleaned and usable version. 
The notebook casts the data types, ensures correct timestamps. Records with no spatial information about the 
pickup are dropped because these cannot be used for later prediction. This missingness is partly due to Chicago's 
privacy protections, which suppress location data for trips in low-frequency census tracts [@chicago_privacy_story]. 
Additionally, illogical records such as trips with an average speed of over 100 mph, negative payments and so 
are dropped. Also excluded are trips which are extremly short in terms of time and distance [^short_trips] as we 
assume that these might be erroneous, quick cancellations or other. Additionally, we exclude trips which are 
extreme in the opposite direction[^long_trips] as these are rare which can be seen in @fig-outlier-filtering.
In total xyz records are reduced to xyz final records. The individual columns can be seen in xyz.

[^short_trips]: 60s or 0.01 miles
[^long_trips]: 200 miles or 3 hours


## Additional Data Sources
To improve the demand prediction additional datasets are added: Holiday, weather, and point-of-interest data. 
An additional Chicago special events dataset was evaluated but it was decided against merging it due to the high
incompletion of the specific time and therefore cannot be matched exactly to the time [@chicago_special_events]. 
The other sets, what the are about and the reason for inclusion are discussed in @tbl-additional-data-sources.

Some weather data is discretized into binary values such as rain or snow to simplify the prediction. Instead
of providing precise value for the prediction, we can just say that the day we want to predict is rainy. On 
the otherhand we lose precision.

| Dataset | What is the data about | Reason for inclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Holidays [@workingdays_holidays] | City, state, bank, and corporate holidays, including the day of the week | Different holiday types affect different rider groups, and trip behavior varies by weekday/weekend |
| Weather[^weather-note] [@open_meteo_weather] | Hourly temperature, rain, snowfall, and wind speed for Chicago | Captures day/night and seasonal weather effects on demand at an hourly resolution matching the trip data |
| Points of Interest [@openstreetmap] | Counts of 8 POI categories (healthcare, education, public services, tourism, nature, amenity, leisure, shops) per census tract and community area | Explains the purpose/attractiveness of a location, helping the model learn location-specific demand patterns |
| Community area boundaries [@chicago_community_areas] | Polygon boundaries of Chicago's community areas | Used to compute community area centroid coordinates as a spatial feature |

: Additional data sources {#tbl-additional-data-sources}



[^weather-note]: We decided for a different weather data source to have hourlyy data.

- Discretized continuous weather variables into binary indicators (`rain`, `strong_rain`, `snow`, `wind`, `strong_wind`) using domain-based thresholds (precipitation intensity, Beaufort scale).
- Merged hourly weather into taxi trips by truncating `trip_start` to the nearest hour; validated match quality (max time delta under 1h).
- Retrieved Points of Interest (POI) from OpenStreetMap via `osmnx`, categorized into 8 groups (healthcare, education, amenity, leisure, shops, public services, tourism, nature).
- Aggregated POI counts per census tract and per community area, exported as CSVs.
- Computed centroid coordinates for census tracts and community areas as spatial features, exported as CSVs.
- Dropped temporary merge columns and exported the combined taxi + holiday + weather dataset to parquet.

## Data Preparation for NN and SVM

- Loaded the merged dataset from notebook 02 and renamed columns for aggregation.
- Built a complete grid of time buckets (1h, 4h, 1d) crossed with spatial units (census tract, community area), so zero-demand periods are represented rather than dropped.
- Aggregated trip counts into demand per time bucket and spatial unit, for both census tract and community area at all three resolutions.
- Visualized trip-count distributions for each aggregation level.
- Merged in previously prepared auxiliary features: holiday flags, POI category counts, centroid coordinates, and time-aggregated weather.
- Engineered cyclic sin/cos features for hour and month at the aggregated level.
- Ran a final null-value check across all six aggregated dataset variants.
- Split each dataset chronologically into train/validation/test (70/15/15) to prevent data leakage.
- Fit a MinMaxScaler on the training set only (POI counts, temperatures, centroid coordinates) and applied it to validation/test; saved fitted scalers to disk per dataset.
- Documented how to reload and reuse the saved scalers in future prediction notebooks.
